items.title: A free complex mapping to a module maps into any resolution, and any two such maps are homotopic
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a map M to N, any resolution of N and any free complex mapping to M, there is a map of complexes lifting the given square, and any two such maps are homotopic (statement lines 17716-17737). The proof does not use a general lifting theorem for projective complexes: it lifts degree by degree using freeness of the terms, and repeats the same device for the difference of two comparison maps, correcting each degree so that the next lift lands in a kernel (proof lines 17739-17763). Seeing that the homotopy is the same lifting argument applied to the difference is the content, and the author writes the induction steps out in both parts. H2.
